doc.title: Urbie Green interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 29, 1995

title: J.J. Johnson
summary: They worked together in the studios; Green admired his clean, neat playing.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Bix Beiderbecke: hearing, copying and remembering him

blocks.x: Did you ever have occasion to work with or be influenced in any way by J.J. Johnson?

Well we worked together a lot, but somehow I don’t think I — I was pretty strong in my own thinking I guess by the time we crossed paths. But we were in the studio about the same time I was in New York. Then he went to California and came back. I admired him greatly, what he does is wonderful, as a musician, such a clean, neat player.
